independence: L2.1 rules (spec/formulas/l21-replay.md v2) re-derived by spec/oracle/l21_oracle.py from the rule text with a full-history window model, plain sets and dictionaries; the lab side calls the real L2.1 functions. Review case l21.req.review.out-of-order and the boundary cases are hand-derived. Written by the same author as the code (not an independent party).

cases.description: new, replay, conflict, closed after count eviction, ahead, invalid
cases.derivation: spec 2.3 rules 2 (replay, conflict), 2.4 count eviction of seq 1 raises H to 1 (rule 3), 40 - T(5) > 16 (rule 4), 0 invalid (rule 1)

cases.description: review section 2: seq 2 at 0, seq 1 at 90, seq 3 at 150 (maxAgeMs 100); retries at 150 and 190
cases.derivation: hand-derived: at 150 receipt 2 (age 150 >= 100) expires and H = 2, so its retry is REQUEST_CLOSED; receipt 1 (age 60) still replays; at 190 it expires too

cases.description: a receipt is live at age maxAgeMs - 1 and closed at age maxAgeMs
receipts expire with time alone (finalNowMs, no further request)
cases.derivation: spec 2.2 at 1200: receipt 1 expires (age 1200), receipt 2 stays (age 700)

cases.description: a far-ahead number is refused and closes nothing; out-of-order numbers in the window execute
cases.derivation: spec 2.3 rule 4 against T = 5; H stays 0

cases.description: only even numbers arrive: no gap membership is kept
cases.derivation: spec 2.4: the five highest receipts remain; H = 30; 31 is closed, 39 executes (above H)

cases.description: an older-numbered live receipt stays replayable after a higher one expires
cases.derivation: spec 2.2: receipt 5 expires at 101, H = 5; receipt 2 still replays (rule 2 before rule 3); 1 and 3 are closed
every limit is a positive safe integer (spec 0)
